title.en: Tech Confidence: Read Your Six Ratings
title.zh: 技术工具信心：六项自评的完整读法

headline.en: A continuous self-rating, with the task and support kept in view
headline.zh: 连续的信心自评，需要连同任务和支持条件一起理解

summary.en: Read the six confidence prompts, their arithmetic, missing-answer policy, contrasting examples and an optional small experiment. No proficiency type or workplace comparison.
summary.zh: 了解六种信心情境、算式、缺答政策、对照例子与可选小实验；不派熟练度类型，不作职场比较。

scoreReading.en: The mean describes only the numeric answers in this attempt. It needs at least four ratings after all six prompts are answered; insufficient coverage never becomes zero or a type.
scoreReading.zh: 均值只描述本次的数字回答。六题全部回应后仍需至少四项数字；资料不足不会变成零分或一种类型。

title.en: Tech Savvy Result: Your Confidence Ratings Explained
title.zh: 技术素养自评结果：六项工具信心的完整读法

description.en: Understand six tool-confidence ratings, raw arithmetic and missing answers, with worked examples and one optional sample task. No skill level or job-fit claim.
description.zh: 读懂六项工具信心自评、原始算式和未评分回答，查看具体算例与一个可选示例任务；不判技能等级，不推断职业适合度。

title.en: A rating of confidence, not a skills demonstration
title.zh: 这是信心自评，不是技能演示

paragraphs.en: These six statements ask how confident you feel about starting, checking, choosing, repeating and discussing small digital tasks. They do not watch you complete those tasks. A confident answer can reflect familiarity, an accessible interface, a useful demonstration or available support. A hesitant answer can reflect an unfamiliar situation rather than inability. Neither answer establishes how accurately or quickly you would perform.
paragraphs.zh: 六句话询问你对开始、核对、选择、重复和讨论小型数字任务有多大把握，并没有观察你实际完成任务。有把握可能来自熟悉、界面容易使用、演示清楚或有人支持；犹豫也可能只是情境陌生，不等于做不到。无论怎样回答，都不能证明操作的准确度或速度。

paragraphs.en: The prompts deliberately avoid a catalogue of fashionable apps. Knowing a product name, owning a device or enjoying new features is not required. Your rating belongs to these particular tasks and the recent situations you considered; it is not a universal identity such as beginner, expert or digital native.
paragraphs.zh: 题目刻意不罗列流行应用。你不需要认得产品名、拥有某种设备，也不需要喜欢新功能。数值只对应这些具体任务和你想到的近期情境，不赋予“新手”“专家”或“数字原住民”等普遍身份。

title.en: How the six answers become one continuous mean
title.zh: 六项回答怎样形成连续均值

paragraphs.en: Each numeric choice contributes its displayed value from 1 to 5. All six prompts need either a number or the explicit no-opportunity / prefer-not-to-rate choice before an attempt finishes. The latter is excluded from the sum and denominator; it is never zero or a presumed low rating. There are no reverse items or hidden weights.
paragraphs.zh: 每个数字选项按显示的1至5计入。六题都需要选择数字或明确的“近期没有机会／不想评价”，本次作答才结束。后一种选择不进入和与分母，既不是零分，也不被假定为较低评价。本版没有反向题或隐藏权重。

paragraphs.en: With at least four numeric responses, divide their sum by their count and round to one decimal. Ratings 2, 3, 4, 4 and 5 plus one unscored response give a sum of 18, five ratings and a mean of 3.6. With only three numeric responses, the page reports insufficient information and shows this general guide. The four-response rule is an editorial completeness policy, not a validated threshold.
paragraphs.zh: 至少四项有数字时，用原始和除以数字项数，再四舍五入保留一位小数。例如2、3、4、4、5及一个不计分回答，原始和为18，数字项数为5，均值为3.6。只有三项数字时，页面显示资料不足，并保留这份通用完整指南。“至少四项”是本版的编辑完整度政策，不是经过验证的阈值。

title.en: Keep the six task contexts in view
title.zh: 把六种任务情境留在视野内

paragraphs.en: Finding a first control and repeating a demonstrated task concern different moments of learning. Checking one step when output is unexpected asks about a bounded comparison. Stating necessary features asks whether you can describe a local need. Explaining a sticking point concerns asking for useful help. Testing a reversible example concerns the confidence to check before relying on a tool.
paragraphs.zh: 找到第一个控件与重复演示任务，对应学习的不同阶段。输出出乎预期时一次核对一步，是有边界的比较；说清必要功能，是描述眼前需要；解释卡点，涉及怎样提出有用的求助；先试可撤销示例，则涉及依赖工具之前是否有把握进行核对。

paragraphs.en: An average does not show which of these situations was easiest to imagine. Revisit your own selected options if the distinction matters. Do not read one overall number as six proven strengths, or treat an unscored task as a weakness. Limited access, a poor demonstration, language and accessibility conditions can change what you have had a chance to try.
paragraphs.zh: 平均数不会说明哪种情境最容易想象。若这些区别与你有关，可以回看自己的具体选项；不要把一个均值读成六种已经证实的长处，也不要把未评分任务当作弱点。接触机会有限、演示不清、语言或可访问性条件，都可能影响你有机会尝试什么。

title.en: Equal means can come from different stories
title.zh: 相同均值可以来自不同经历

paragraphs.en: Suppose one person rates four familiar tasks as 4 and leaves two unfamiliar tasks unscored. Another rates all six tasks as 4. Both means are 4.0, while their coverage differs. Or compare 1, 2, 3, 4, 4, 4 with six 3s: both sums are 18 and both means 3.0, yet the individual patterns differ. The page keeps the numeric-response count visible for this reason.
paragraphs.zh: 假设一人把四项熟悉任务都评为4，另外两项因陌生而不评分；另一人六项都评为4。两者均值都是4.0，覆盖范围却不同。再比较1、2、3、4、4、4与六个3：两组和均为18、均值均为3.0，逐项模式仍不同。因此页面会同时保留数字项数。

paragraphs.en: There is no workplace benchmark, percentile or meaningful-change cutoff here. A later difference may follow a new task, different support or a changed interpretation of an anchor. You may record that context privately if useful; the quiz cannot separate those possibilities or certify progress from a number alone.
paragraphs.zh: 这里没有职场基准、百分位或有意义变化的界线。以后数值不同，可能因为换了任务、支持条件变了，或对选项的理解不同。若有用，你可以私下记下情境；本测试无法区分这些原因，也不能只凭数值认证进步。

title.en: One optional experiment with a harmless example
title.zh: 可选：用无敏感信息的小例子试一次

paragraphs.en: Choose one task you actually want to do, such as arranging three invented appointments in a sample calendar. Write the intended result in one sentence, try it with dummy entries, then compare the visible output with that sentence. If you get stuck, note the exact step rather than concluding that you are bad at technology. Asking someone to explain one control is an equally valid next step.
paragraphs.zh: 选一项你确实想做的小任务，例如在示例日历中排列三个虚构约会。先用一句话写下预期结果，用虚构条目尝试，再对照屏幕输出与那句话。若卡住，记下具体步骤，不必据此认定自己“不擅长技术”。请人解释一个控件，也是同样有效的下一步。

paragraphs.en: This is a suggestion for comparison, not homework, a performance test or a reason to buy software. Keep private files, credentials and real account changes out of the example. A high rating does not make an unfamiliar tool safe; a low rating does not oblige you to practise. You can finish with the reading alone.
paragraphs.zh: 这只是可选的比较办法，不是作业、表现测试或购买软件的理由。示例不应包含私密文件、凭据或真实账户变更。较高自评不能证明陌生工具安全，较低自评也不要求你练习。只读完这份说明就结束，也完全可以。

title.en: Privacy, choice and the limits of this reading
title.zh: 隐私、选择与本篇读法的界限

paragraphs.en: The website calculates the result in the page. Optional progress saving uses this tab’s session storage, expires after 24 hours and clears on completion, retake or exit-and-clear. Copying contains the test title, a general reading label and a public link, without your six answers, sum or mean. The public guide can be read before taking the quiz.
paragraphs.zh: 网站在页面中计算结果。可选进度保存使用本标签页的会话存储，24小时后失效，完成、重测或退出清除后删除。复制内容只有测试标题、通用读法名称和公开链接，不含六项回答、原始和或均值。无需答题，也能先读这份完整公开指南。

paragraphs.en: This original short self-report has no established psychometric validation, cross-language equivalence or population norms. It does not measure general digital competence, anxiety, intelligence, job readiness, salary potential or suitability for recruitment. If you need evidence of a particular skill, a clearly defined task and its checked output answer a different question; this confidence mean cannot substitute for that evidence.
paragraphs.zh: 这份原创简短自评尚未建立心理测量验证、跨语言等值或人群常模。它不测量一般数字能力、焦虑、智力、工作就绪度、薪资潜力或招聘适合度。若你需要某项具体技能的证据，定义明确的任务及经核对的输出回答的是另一个问题；本篇的信心均值不能替代这类证据。
